title: Read a Greek Sign
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Transliterate twelve Greek signs from the route into Latin letters, with a letter key, trap-letter hints after a first miss, and a letter-by-letter breakdown.

learningObjectives: Use the Greek letter table to transliterate twelve Greek signs from the route into Latin letters, with at least 10 of 12 correct within two attempts each.
prerequisites: The Greek capital letters and their sign transliterations
The letter pairs ΟΥ, ΑΙ, ΕΙ and ΟΙ

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Practice with typed answers, graduated hints and immediate feedback
keyQuestions: Which letters on this sign look like ours but are not?
Which letter pairs make a single sound?
commonMisconceptions: Η is the consonant h (it is the vowel i).
Χ is x (it is a throaty h, written ch).
Υ is u (alone it is y, sounding ee).
Λ is an upside-down v (it is l).
Greek signs must be read letter by letter for pronunciation (pairs like ΕΙ and ΟΥ make one sound).
assessmentOpportunities: Signs read within two tries (mastery: 10 of 12).
Tally of trap letters in the signs missed at least once.
